title: Measure early readers' rate, not only accuracy
statement: For early readers, measure oral reading rate as well as accuracy, since rate tracks standardized reading scores more closely, and a reader can be accurate yet slow.
example: In one grade-2 cohort of 51 learners, words correct per minute correlated 0.43 with the standardized reading percentile, against 0.20 for accuracy.
detail: A proxy check on 51 second-grade learners with at least five fluency attempts and a standardized reading score correlated each fluency measure with the external percentile: words correct per minute at r = 0.43, accuracy at r = 0.20 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md`, lines 58-64). A pedagogy red team on the same course had argued that accuracy is the least sensitive fluency measure, that rate and prosody are what predict comprehension, and that a cohort can be 86% accurate and still read slowly, word by word (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-2-pedagogy.md`, line 62).
against: Only a third of the fluency learners had a score that could be joined, hence n = 51 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md`, line 73). Fluency practice also transfers only moderately: in a meta-analysis of repeated reading, the effect was smallest, .35, on comprehension outcomes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`, line 469).

evidence.quote: was run on the 51 G2 students with both ≥5 fluency attempts and a MAP record:
Accuracy is the *least* sensitive fluency measure; the fluency constructs that actually predict comprehension are **rate (WCPM) and prosody**
A cohort can be 86% accurate and still dysfluent (slow, word-by-word, no prosody) — and dysfluent readers comprehend poorly *even when accurate*.
Caveats: n=51 (only ⅓ of fluency students had a joinable MAP record)
It was largest (.55) when the outcome measure was word recognition, next largest (.44) with a fluency measure, and smallest (.35) with a comprehension outcome measure.

citations.ref: Reading for Understanding: Toward an R&D Program in Reading Comprehension (RAND, 2002)
